lines.text: Enter Lord Bardolph.

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Who keeps the gate here, ho?

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: The Porter opens the gate.

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Where is the Earl?

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: What shall I say you are?

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Tell thou the Earl

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: That the Lord Bardolph doth attend him here.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: His lordship is walk’d forth into the orchard.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: Please it your honour knock but at the gate,

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: And he himself will answer.
Enter Northumberland.

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Here comes the Earl.
[_Exit Porter._]

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: What news, Lord Bardolph? Every minute now

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Should be the father of some stratagem.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: The times are wild; contention, like a horse

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Full of high feeding, madly hath broke loose

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And bears down all before him.

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Noble earl,

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: I bring you certain news from Shrewsbury.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Good, an God will!

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: As good as heart can wish.

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: The King is almost wounded to the death;

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: And, in the fortune of my lord your son,

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Prince Harry slain outright; and both the Blunts

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Kill’d by the hand of Douglas; young Prince John

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: And Westmoreland and Stafford fled the field;

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: And Harry Monmouth’s brawn, the hulk Sir John,

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Is prisoner to your son. O, such a day,

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: So fought, so follow’d and so fairly won,

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Came not till now to dignify the times

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Since Caesar’s fortunes!

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: How is this derived?

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Saw you the field? Came you from Shrewsbury?

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: I spake with one, my lord, that came from thence,

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: A gentleman well bred and of good name,

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: That freely render’d me these news for true.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Here comes my servant Travers, whom I sent

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: On Tuesday last to listen after news.
Enter Travers.

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: My lord, I over-rode him on the way,

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: And he is furnish’d with no certainties

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: More than he haply may retail from me.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Now, Travers, what good tidings comes with you?

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: My lord, Sir John Umfrevile turn’d me back

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: With joyful tidings, and, being better horsed,

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: Out-rode me. After him came spurring hard

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: A gentleman, almost forspent with speed,

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: That stopp’d by me to breathe his bloodied horse.

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: He ask’d the way to Chester, and of him

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: I did demand what news from Shrewsbury.

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: He told me that rebellion had bad luck

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: And that young Harry Percy’s spur was cold.

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: With that he gave his able horse the head,

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: And bending forward struck his armed heels

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: Against the panting sides of his poor jade

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: Up to the rowel-head, and starting so

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: He seem’d in running to devour the way,

lines.speaker: TRAVERS
lines.text: Staying no longer question.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Ha? Again:

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Said he young Harry Percy’s spur was cold?

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Of Hotspur, Coldspur? That rebellion

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Had met ill luck?

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: My lord, I’ll tell you what:

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: If my young lord your son have not the day,

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Upon mine honour, for a silken point

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: I’ll give my barony, never talk of it.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Why should that gentleman that rode by Travers

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Give then such instances of loss?

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Who, he?

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: He was some hilding fellow that had stolen

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: The horse he rode on, and, upon my life,

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Spoke at a venture. Look, here comes more news.
Enter Morton.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Yea, this man’s brow, like to a title-leaf,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Foretells the nature of a tragic volume.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: So looks the strand whereon the imperious flood

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Hath left a witness’d usurpation.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Say, Morton, didst thou come from Shrewsbury?

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: I ran from Shrewsbury, my noble lord,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Where hateful death put on his ugliest mask

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: To fright our party.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: How doth my son and brother?

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Thou tremblest, and the whiteness in thy cheek

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Is apter than thy tongue to tell thy errand.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Even such a man, so faint, so spiritless,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: So dull, so dread in look, so woe-begone,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Drew Priam’s curtain in the dead of night,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And would have told him half his Troy was burnt;

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: But Priam found the fire ere he his tongue,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And I my Percy’s death ere thou report’st it.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: This thou wouldst say: “Your son did thus and thus;

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Your brother thus; so fought the noble Douglas”

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Stopping my greedy ear with their bold deeds:

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: But in the end, to stop my ear indeed,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Thou hast a sigh to blow away this praise,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Ending with “Brother, son, and all are dead.”

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Douglas is living, and your brother, yet;

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: But, for my lord your son—

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Why, he is dead.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: See what a ready tongue suspicion hath!

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: He that but fears the thing he would not know

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Hath by instinct knowledge from others’ eyes

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: That what he fear’d is chanced. Yet speak, Morton;

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Tell thou an earl his divination lies,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And I will take it as a sweet disgrace

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And make thee rich for doing me such wrong.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: You are too great to be by me gainsaid,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Your spirit is too true, your fears too certain.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Yet, for all this, say not that Percy’s dead.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: I see a strange confession in thine eye.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Thou shakest thy head and hold’st it fear or sin

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: To speak a truth. If he be slain, say so.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: The tongue offends not that reports his death;

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And he doth sin that doth belie the dead,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Not he which says the dead is not alive.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Yet the first bringer of unwelcome news

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Hath but a losing office, and his tongue

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Sounds ever after as a sullen bell,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Remember’d tolling a departing friend.

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: I cannot think, my lord, your son is dead.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: I am sorry I should force you to believe

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: That which I would to God I had not seen;

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: But these mine eyes saw him in bloody state,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Rend’ring faint quittance, wearied and outbreathed,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: To Harry Monmouth, whose swift wrath beat down

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: The never-daunted Percy to the earth,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: From whence with life he never more sprung up.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: In few, his death, whose spirit lent a fire

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Even to the dullest peasant in his camp,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Being bruited once, took fire and heat away

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: From the best-temper’d courage in his troops;

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: For from his metal was his party steel’d,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Which once in him abated, all the rest

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Turn’d on themselves, like dull and heavy lead.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: And as the thing that’s heavy in itself

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Upon enforcement flies with greatest speed,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: So did our men, heavy in Hotspur’s loss,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Lend to this weight such lightness with their fear

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: That arrows fled not swifter toward their aim

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Than did our soldiers, aiming at their safety,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Fly from the field. Then was that noble Worcester

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Too soon ta’en prisoner; and that furious Scot,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: The bloody Douglas, whose well-labouring sword

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Had three times slain th’ appearance of the King,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Gan vail his stomach and did grace the shame

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Of those that turn’d their backs, and in his flight,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Stumbling in fear, was took. The sum of all

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Is that the King hath won, and hath sent out

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: A speedy power to encounter you, my lord,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Under the conduct of young Lancaster

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: And Westmoreland. This is the news at full.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: For this I shall have time enough to mourn.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: In poison there is physic; and these news,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Having been well, that would have made me sick,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Being sick, have in some measure made me well.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And as the wretch, whose fever-weaken’d joints,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Like strengthless hinges, buckle under life,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Impatient of his fit, breaks like a fire

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Out of his keeper’s arms, even so my limbs,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Weaken’d with grief, being now enraged with grief,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Are thrice themselves. Hence, therefore, thou nice crutch!

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: A scaly gauntlet now with joints of steel

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Must glove this hand. And hence, thou sickly coif!

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Thou art a guard too wanton for the head

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Which princes, flesh’d with conquest, aim to hit.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Now bind my brows with iron, and approach

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: The ragged’st hour that time and spite dare bring

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: To frown upon th’ enraged Northumberland!

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Let heaven kiss earth! Now let not Nature’s hand

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Keep the wild flood confined! Let order die!

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And let this world no longer be a stage

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: To feed contention in a lingering act;

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: But let one spirit of the first-born Cain

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Reign in all bosoms, that, each heart being set

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: On bloody courses, the rude scene may end,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And darkness be the burier of the dead!

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: This strained passion doth you wrong, my lord.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Sweet earl, divorce not wisdom from your honour.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: The lives of all your loving complices

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Lean on your health; the which, if you give o’er

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: To stormy passion, must perforce decay.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: You cast th’ event of war, my noble lord,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: And summ’d the account of chance, before you said

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: “Let us make head.” It was your presurmise

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: That in the dole of blows your son might drop.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: You knew he walk’d o’er perils, on an edge,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: More likely to fall in than to get o’er.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: You were advised his flesh was capable

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Of wounds and scars, and that his forward spirit

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Would lift him where most trade of danger ranged.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Yet did you say “Go forth;” and none of this,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Though strongly apprehended, could restrain

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: The stiff-borne action. What hath then befall’n,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Or what hath this bold enterprise brought forth,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: More than that being which was like to be?

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: We all that are engaged to this loss

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Knew that we ventured on such dangerous seas

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: That if we wrought out life ’twas ten to one;

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: And yet we ventured, for the gain proposed

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Choked the respect of likely peril fear’d;

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: And since we are o’erset, venture again.

lines.speaker: LORD BARDOLPH
lines.text: Come, we will put forth, body and goods.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: ’Tis more than time. And, my most noble lord,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: I hear for certain, and dare speak the truth:

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: The gentle Archbishop of York is up

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: With well-appointed powers. He is a man

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Who with a double surety binds his followers.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: My lord your son had only but the corpse,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: But shadows and the shows of men, to fight;

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: For that same word, “rebellion” did divide

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: The action of their bodies from their souls,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: And they did fight with queasiness, constrain’d,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: As men drink potions, that their weapons only

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Seem’d on our side; but, for their spirits and souls,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: This word, “rebellion,” it had froze them up,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: As fish are in a pond. But now the bishop

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Turns insurrection to religion.

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Supposed sincere and holy in his thoughts,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: He’s follow’d both with body and with mind,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: And doth enlarge his rising with the blood

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Of fair King Richard, scraped from Pomfret stones;

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Derives from heaven his quarrel and his cause;

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Tells them he doth bestride a bleeding land,

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: Gasping for life under great Bolingbroke;

lines.speaker: MORTON
lines.text: And more and less do flock to follow him.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: I knew of this before; but, to speak truth,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: This present grief had wiped it from my mind.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Go in with me, and counsel every man

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: The aptest way for safety and revenge.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Get posts and letters, and make friends with speed.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Never so few, and never yet more need.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Falstaff, with his Page bearing his sword and buckler.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Sirrah, you giant, what says the doctor to my water?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: He said, sir, the water itself was a good healthy water; but, for the

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: party that owed it, he might have moe diseases than he knew for.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Men of all sorts take a pride to gird at me. The brain of this

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: foolish-compounded clay, man, is not able to invent anything that tends

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: to laughter more than I invent, or is invented on me. I am not only

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: witty in myself, but the cause that wit is in other men. I do here walk

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: before thee like a sow that hath overwhelmed all her litter but one. If

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the Prince put thee into my service for any other reason than to set me

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: off, why then I have no judgement. Thou whoreson mandrake, thou art

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: fitter to be worn in my cap than to wait at my heels. I was never

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: manned with an agate till now, but I will inset you neither in gold nor

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: silver, but in vile apparel, and send you back again to your master,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: for a jewel,—the juvenal, the Prince your master, whose chin is not yet

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: fledge. I will sooner have a beard grow in the palm of my hand than he

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shall get one off his cheek; and yet he will not stick to say his face

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: is a face-royal. God may finish it when He will, ’tis not a hair amiss

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: yet. He may keep it still at a face-royal, for a barber shall never

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: earn sixpence out of it. And yet he’ll be crowing as if he had writ man

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ever since his father was a bachelor. He may keep his own grace, but

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: he’s almost out of mine, I can assure him. What said Master Dommelton

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: about the satin for my short cloak and my slops?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: He said, sir, you should procure him better assurance than Bardolph. He

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: would not take his band and yours, he liked not the security.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Let him be damned like the glutton! Pray God his tongue be hotter! A

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: whoreson Achitophel! A rascally yea-forsooth knave, to bear a gentleman

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: in hand, and then stand upon security! The whoreson smooth-pates do now

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: wear nothing but high shoes and bunches of keys at their girdles; and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: if a man is through with them in honest taking up, then they must stand

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: upon security. I had as lief they would put ratsbane in my mouth as

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: offer to stop it with security. I looked he should have sent me two and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: twenty yards of satin, as I am a true knight, and he sends me

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: “security”. Well, he may sleep in security, for he hath the horn of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: abundance, and the lightness of his wife shines through it; and yet

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cannot he see, though he have his own lanthorn to light him. Where’s

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Bardolph?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: He’s gone into Smithfield to buy your worship a horse.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I bought him in Paul’s, and he’ll buy me a horse in Smithfield. An I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: could get me but a wife in the stews, I were manned, horsed, and wived.

lines.text: Sir, here comes the nobleman that committed the Prince for striking him

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Sir John!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What! A young knave, and begging! Is there not wars? Is there not

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: employment? Doth not the King lack subjects? Do not the rebels need

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: soldiers? Though it be a shame to be on any side but one, it is worse

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shame to beg than to be on the worst side, were it worse than the name

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: of rebellion can tell how to make it.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: You mistake me, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Why, sir, did I say you were an honest man? Setting my knighthood and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: my soldiership aside, I had lied in my throat if I had said so.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: I pray you, sir, then set your knighthood and your soldiership aside,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: and give me leave to tell you, you lie in your throat, if you say I am

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: any other than an honest man.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I give thee leave to tell me so? I lay aside that which grows to me? If

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: thou get’st any leave of me, hang me; if thou tak’st leave, thou wert

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: better be hanged. You hunt counter. Hence! Avaunt!

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Sir, my lord would speak with you.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Sir John Falstaff, a word with you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My good lord! God give your lordship good time of day. I am glad to see

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: your lordship abroad. I heard say your lordship was sick. I hope your

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: lordship goes abroad by advice. Your lordship, though not clean past

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: your youth, hath yet some smack of age in you, some relish of the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: saltness of time; and I most humbly beseech your lordship to have a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: reverend care of your health.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Sir John, I sent for you before your expedition to Shrewsbury.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: An ’t please your lordship, I hear his Majesty is returned with some

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: discomfort from Wales.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: I talk not of his Majesty. You would not come when I sent for you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: And I hear, moreover, his Highness is fallen into this same whoreson

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: apoplexy.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Well, God mend him! I pray you let me speak with you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: This apoplexy, as I take it, is a kind of lethargy, an ’t please your

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: lordship, a kind of sleeping in the blood, a whoreson tingling.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: What tell you me of it? Be it as it is.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: It hath it original from much grief, from study and perturbation of the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: brain. I have read the cause of his effects in Galen. It is a kind of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: deafness.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: I think you are fallen into the disease, for you hear not what I say to

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Very well, my lord, very well. Rather, an ’t please you, it is the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: disease of not listening, the malady of not marking, that I am troubled

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: withal.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: To punish you by the heels would amend the attention of your ears, and

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: I care not if I do become your physician.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I am as poor as Job, my lord, but not so patient. Your lordship may

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: minister the potion of imprisonment to me in respect of poverty; but

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: how I should be your patient to follow your prescriptions, the wise may

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: make some dram of a scruple, or indeed a scruple itself.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: I sent for you, when there were matters against you for your life, to

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: come speak with me.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: As I was then advised by my learned counsel in the laws of this

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: land-service, I did not come.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Well, the truth is, Sir John, you live in great infamy.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: He that buckles himself in my belt cannot live in less.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Your means are very slender, and your waste is great.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I would it were otherwise, I would my means were greater and my waist

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: slenderer.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: You have misled the youthful prince.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: The young prince hath misled me. I am the fellow with the great belly,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and he my dog.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Well, I am loath to gall a new-healed wound. Your day’s service at

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Shrewsbury hath a little gilded over your night’s exploit on Gad’s

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Hill. You may thank th’ unquiet time for your quiet o’er-posting that

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: action.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My lord!

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: But since all is well, keep it so: wake not a sleeping wolf.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: To wake a wolf is as bad as smell a fox.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: What! You are as a candle, the better part burnt out.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: A wassail candle, my lord, all tallow. If I did say of wax, my growth

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: would approve the truth.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: There is not a white hair in your face but should have his effect of

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: gravity.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: His effect of gravy, gravy, gravy.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: You follow the young prince up and down, like his ill angel.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Not so, my lord, your ill angel is light, but I hope he that looks upon

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: me will take me without weighing. And yet in some respects, I grant, I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cannot go. I cannot tell. Virtue is of so little regard in these

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: costermongers’ times that true valour is turned bearherd; pregnancy is

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: made a tapster, and hath his quick wit wasted in giving reckonings. All

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the other gifts appertinent to man, as the malice of this age shapes

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: them, are not worth a gooseberry. You that are old consider not the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: capacities of us that are young; you do measure the heat of our livers

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: with the bitterness of your galls, and we that are in the vaward of our

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: youth, I must confess, are wags too.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Do you set down your name in the scroll of youth, that are written down

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: old with all the characters of age? Have you not a moist eye, a dry

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: hand, a yellow cheek, a white beard, a decreasing leg, an increasing

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: belly? Is not your voice broken, your wind short, your chin double,

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: your wit single, and every part about you blasted with antiquity? And

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: will you yet call yourself young? Fie, fie, fie, Sir John!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: white head and something a round belly. For my voice, I have lost it

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: will not. The truth is, I am only old in judgement and understanding;

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the money, and have at him! For the box of the ear that the Prince gave

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: lord. I have checked him for it, and the young lion repents. Marry, not

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: in ashes and sackcloth, but in new silk and old sack.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Well, God send the Prince a better companion!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: God send the companion a better prince! I cannot rid my hands of him.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Well, the King hath severed you and Prince Harry. I hear you are going

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: with Lord John of Lancaster against the Archbishop and the Earl of

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Northumberland.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Yea, I thank your pretty sweet wit for it. But look you pray, all you

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: that kiss my lady Peace at home, that our armies join not in a hot day;

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: for, by the Lord, I take but two shirts out with me, and I mean not to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: sweat extraordinarily. If it be a hot day, and I brandish anything but

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: a bottle, I would I might never spit white again. There is not a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: dangerous action can peep out his head but I am thrust upon it. Well, I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cannot last ever. But it was alway yet the trick of our English nation,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: if they have a good thing, to make it too common. If ye will needs say

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I am an old man, you should give me rest. I would to God my name were

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: not so terrible to the enemy as it is. I were better to be eaten to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: death with a rust than to be scoured to nothing with perpetual motion.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Well, be honest, be honest, and God bless your expedition!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Will your lordship lend me a thousand pound to furnish me forth?

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Not a penny, not a penny; you are too impatient to bear crosses. Fare

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: you well: commend me to my cousin Westmoreland.
[_Exeunt Chief Justice and Servant._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF

lines.text: Sir?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: this letter to my Lord of Lancaster; this to the Prince; this to the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Earl of Westmoreland; and this to old Mistress Ursula, whom I have

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: weekly sworn to marry since I perceived the first white hair of my

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: chin. About it. You know where to find me. [_Exit Page_.] A pox of this

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: gout! or a gout of this pox! for the one or the other plays the rogue

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: with my great toe. ’Tis no matter if I do halt; I have the wars for my

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: colour, and my pension shall seem the more reasonable. A good wit will

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: make use of anything. I will turn diseases to commodity.
[_Exit._]

lines.text: fubbed off, and fubbed off, and fubbed off, from this day to that day,

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: that it is a shame to be thought on. There is no honesty in such

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: dealing, unless a woman should be made an ass and a beast, to bear

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: every knave’s wrong. Yonder he comes, and that arrant malmsey-nose

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: knave, Bardolph, with him. Do your offices, do your offices, Master

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Fang and Master Snare, do me, do me, do me your offices.
Enter Falstaff, Bardolph and Page.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: How now, whose mare’s dead? What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: FANG
lines.text: Sir John, I arrest you at the suit of Mistress Quickly.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Away, varlets! Draw, Bardolph! Cut me off the villain’s head. Throw the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: quean in the channel.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Throw me in the channel? I’ll throw thee in the channel. Wilt thou,

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: wilt thou, thou bastardly rogue? Murder, murder! Ah, thou honeysuckle

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: villain, wilt thou kill God’s officers and the King’s? Ah, thou

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: honeyseed rogue, thou art a honeyseed, a man-queller, and a

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: woman-queller.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Keep them off, Bardolph.

lines.speaker: FANG
lines.text: A rescue! A rescue!

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Good people, bring a rescue or two. Thou wo’t, wo’t thou? Thou wo’t,

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: wo’t ta? Do, do, thou rogue! Do, thou hempseed!

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Away, you scullion! you rampallian! you fustilarian! I’ll tickle your

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: catastrophe.
Enter the Lord Chief Justice and his men.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: What is the matter? Keep the peace here, ho!

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Good my lord, be good to me. I beseech you stand to me.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: How now, Sir John? What are you brawling here?

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Doth this become your place, your time and business?

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: You should have been well on your way to York.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Stand from him, fellow. Wherefore hang’st thou upon him?

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: O my most worshipful lord, an’t please your Grace, I am a poor widow of

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Eastcheap, and he is arrested at my suit.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: For what sum?

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: It is more than for some, my lord; it is for all, all I have. He hath

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: eaten me out of house and home. He hath put all my substance into that

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: fat belly of his: but I will have some of it out again, or I will ride

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: thee o’ nights like the mare.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I think I am as like to ride the mare if I have any vantage of ground

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: to get up.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: How comes this, Sir John? Fie! what man of good temper would endure

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: this tempest of exclamation? Are you not ashamed to enforce a poor

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: widow to so rough a course to come by her own?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What is the gross sum that I owe thee?

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Marry, if thou wert an honest man, thyself and the money too. Thou

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: didst swear to me upon a parcel-gilt goblet, sitting in my Dolphin

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: chamber, at the round table, by a sea-coal fire, upon Wednesday in

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Wheeson week, when the Prince broke thy head for liking his father to a

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: singing-man of Windsor, thou didst swear to me then, as I was washing

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: thy wound, to marry me and make me my lady thy wife. Canst thou deny

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: it? Did not goodwife Keech, the butcher’s wife, come in then and call

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: me gossip Quickly? coming in to borrow a mess of vinegar, telling us

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: she had a good dish of prawns, whereby thou didst desire to eat some,

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: whereby I told thee they were ill for green wound? And didst thou not,

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: when she was gone downstairs, desire me to be no more so familiarity

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: with such poor people, saying that ere long they should call me madam?

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: And didst thou not kiss me, and bid me fetch thee thirty shillings? I

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: put thee now to thy book-oath. Deny it, if thou canst.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My lord, this is a poor mad soul, and she says up and down the town

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: that her eldest son is like you. She hath been in good case, and the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: truth is, poverty hath distracted her. But for these foolish officers,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I beseech you I may have redress against them.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Sir John, Sir John, I am well acquainted with your manner of wrenching

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: the true cause the false way. It is not a confident brow, nor the

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: throng of words that come with such more than impudent sauciness from

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: you, can thrust me from a level consideration. You have, as it appears

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: to me, practised upon the easy-yielding spirit of this woman, and made

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: her serve your uses both in purse and in person.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Yea, in truth, my lord.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Pray thee, peace. Pay her the debt you owe her, and unpay the villany

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: you have done with her. The one you may do with sterling money, and the

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: other with current repentance.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My lord, I will not undergo this sneap without reply. You call

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: honourable boldness impudent sauciness; if a man will make curtsy and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: say nothing, he is virtuous. No, my lord, my humble duty remembered, I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: will not be your suitor. I say to you, I do desire deliverance from

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: these officers, being upon hasty employment in the King’s affairs.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: You speak as having power to do wrong; but answer in th’ effect of your

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: reputation, and satisfy the poor woman.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Come hither, hostess.
Enter Gower.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Now, Master Gower, what news?

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: The King, my lord, and Harry Prince of Wales

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Are near at hand: the rest the paper tells.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: As I am a gentleman.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Faith, you said so before.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: As I am a gentleman. Come, no more words of it.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: By this heavenly ground I tread on, I must be fain to pawn both my

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: plate and the tapestry of my dining-chambers.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Glasses, glasses, is the only drinking. And for thy walls, a pretty

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: slight drollery, or the story of the Prodigal, or the German hunting in

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: waterwork, is worth a thousand of these bed-hangers and these

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: fly-bitten tapestries. Let it be ten pound, if thou canst. Come, an

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ’twere not for thy humours, there’s not a better wench in England. Go,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: wash thy face, and draw the action. Come, thou must not be in this

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: humour with me; dost not know me? Come, come, I know thou wast set on

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: to this.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Pray thee, Sir John, let it be but twenty nobles. I’ faith, I am loath

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: to pawn my plate, so God save me, la!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Let it alone, I’ll make other shift: you’ll be a fool still.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Well, you shall have it, though I pawn my gown. I hope you’ll come to

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: supper. You’ll pay me all together?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Will I live? [_To Bardolph_.] Go, with her, with her. Hook on, hook on.

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: Will you have Doll Tearsheet meet you at supper?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: No more words, let’s have her.
[_Exeunt Hostess, Fang, Snare, Bardolph and Page._]

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: I have heard better news.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What’s the news, my lord?

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Where lay the King tonight?

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: At Basingstoke, my lord.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I hope, my lord, all’s well. What is the news, my lord?

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Come all his forces back?

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: No, fifteen hundred foot, five hundred horse

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Are march’d up to my Lord of Lancaster,

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: Against Northumberland and the Archbishop.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Comes the King back from Wales, my noble lord?

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: You shall have letters of me presently.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Come, go along with me, good Master Gower.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My lord!

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Master Gower, shall I entreat you with me to dinner?

lines.speaker: GOWER
lines.text: I must wait upon my good lord here, I thank you, good Sir John.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Sir John, you loiter here too long, being you are to take soldiers up

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: in counties as you go.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Will you sup with me, Master Gower?

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: What foolish master taught you these manners, Sir John?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Master Gower, if they become me not, he was a fool that taught them me.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: This is the right fencing grace, my lord; tap for tap, and so part

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: fair.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Now the Lord lighten thee, thou art a great fool.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Prince Henry and Poins.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Before God, I am exceeding weary.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Is ’t come to that? I had thought weariness durst not have attached one

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: of so high blood.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Faith, it does me, though it discolours the complexion of my greatness

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: to acknowledge it. Doth it not show vilely in me to desire small beer?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Why, a prince should not be so loosely studied as to remember so weak a

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: composition.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Belike then my appetite was not princely got, for, by my troth, I do

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: now remember the poor creature small beer. But indeed, these humble

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: considerations make me out of love with my greatness. What a disgrace

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: is it to me to remember thy name! or to know thy face tomorrow! or to

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: take note how many pair of silk stockings thou hast—viz. these, and

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: those that were thy peach-coloured ones! or to bear the inventory of

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: thy shirts, as, one for superfluity, and another for use! But that the

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: tennis-court keeper knows better than I, for it is a low ebb of linen

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: with thee when thou keepest not racket there; as thou hast not done a

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: great while, because the rest of thy low countries have made a shift to

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: eat up thy holland. And God knows whether those that bawl out of the

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: ruins of thy linen shall inherit his kingdom: but the midwives say the

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: children are not in the fault; whereupon the world increases, and

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: kindreds are mightily strengthened.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: How ill it follows, after you have laboured so hard, you should talk so

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: idly! Tell me, how many good young princes would do so, their fathers

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: being so sick as yours at this time is?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Shall I tell thee one thing, Poins?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Yes, faith, and let it be an excellent good thing.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: It shall serve among wits of no higher breeding than thine.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Go to, I stand the push of your one thing that you will tell.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Marry, I tell thee it is not meet that I should be sad, now my father

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: is sick; albeit I could tell to thee, as to one it pleases me, for

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: fault of a better, to call my friend, I could be sad, and sad indeed

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: too.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Very hardly upon such a subject.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: By this hand, thou thinkest me as far in the devil’s book as thou and

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Falstaff for obduracy and persistency. Let the end try the man. But I

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: tell thee, my heart bleeds inwardly that my father is so sick; and

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: keeping such vile company as thou art hath in reason taken from me all

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: ostentation of sorrow.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: The reason?

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What wouldst thou think of me if I should weep?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: I would think thee a most princely hypocrite.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: It would be every man’s thought; and thou art a blessed fellow to think

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: as every man thinks. Never a man’s thought in the world keeps the

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: roadway better than thine: every man would think me an hypocrite

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: indeed. And what accites your most worshipful thought to think so?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Why, because you have been so lewd and so much engraffed to Falstaff.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And to thee.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: By this light, I am well spoke on; I can hear it with mine own ears.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: The worst that they can say of me is that I am a second brother, and

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: that I am a proper fellow of my hands; and those two things, I confess,

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: I cannot help. By the mass, here comes Bardolph.
Enter Bardolph and Page.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And the boy that I gave Falstaff. He had him from me Christian, and

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: look if the fat villain have not transformed him ape.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: God save your Grace!

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And yours, most noble Bardolph!

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Come, you virtuous ass, you bashful fool, must you be blushing?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Wherefore blush you now? What a maidenly man-at-arms are you become! Is

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: ’t such a matter to get a pottle-pot’s maidenhead?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: He calls me e’en now, my lord, through a red lattice, and I could

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: discern no part of his face from the window. At last I spied his eyes,

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: and methought he had made two holes in the ale-wife’s new petticoat and

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: so peeped through.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Has not the boy profited?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Away, you whoreson upright rabbit, away!

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Away, you rascally Althaea’s dream, away!

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Instruct us, boy; what dream, boy?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Marry, my lord, Althaea dreamt she was delivered of a firebrand; and

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: therefore I call him her dream.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: A crown’s worth of good interpretation. There ’tis, boy.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: O, that this blossom could be kept from cankers! Well, there is

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: sixpence to preserve thee.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: An you do not make him be hanged among you, the gallows shall have

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: wrong.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: And how doth thy master, Bardolph?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Well, my lord. He heard of your Grace’s coming to town. There’s a

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: letter for you.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Delivered with good respect. And how doth the martlemas, your master?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: In bodily health, sir.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Marry, the immortal part needs a physician, but that moves not him.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Though that be sick, it dies not.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: I do allow this wen to be as familiar with me as my dog, and he holds

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: his place, for look you how he writes.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: “John Falstaff, knight,” Every man must know that, as oft as

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: he has occasion to name himself: even like those that are kin to the

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: King, for they never prick their finger but they say, “There’s some of

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: the King’s blood spilt.” “How comes that?” says he that takes upon him

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: not to conceive. The answer is as ready as a borrower’s cap, “I am the

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: King’s poor cousin, sir.”

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Nay, they will be kin to us, or they will fetch it from Japhet. But to

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: the letter: “Sir John Falstaff, knight, to the son of the King, nearest

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: his father, Harry Prince of Wales, greeting.”

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Why, this is a certificate.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Peace! “I will imitate the honourable Romans in brevity.”

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: He sure means brevity in breath, short-winded.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: “I commend me to thee, I commend thee, and I leave thee. Be not too

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: familiar with Poins, for he misuses thy favours so much that he swears

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: thou art to marry his sister Nell. Repent at idle times as thou mayst,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: and so, farewell.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Thine by yea and no, which is as much as to say, as thou usest him—Jack

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Falstaff with my familiars, John with my brothers and sisters, and Sir

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: John with all Europe.”

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: My lord, I’ll steep this letter in sack and make him eat it.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: That’s to make him eat twenty of his words. But do you use me thus,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Ned? Must I marry your sister?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: God send the wench no worse fortune! But I never said so.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Well, thus we play the fools with the time, and the spirits of the wise

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: sit in the clouds and mock us. Is your master here in London?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Yea, my lord.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Where sups he? Doth the old boar feed in the old frank?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: At the old place, my lord, in Eastcheap.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What company?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Ephesians, my lord, of the old church.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Sup any women with him?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: None, my lord, but old Mistress Quickly and Mistress Doll Tearsheet.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: What pagan may that be?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: A proper gentlewoman, sir, and a kinswoman of my master’s.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Even such kin as the parish heifers are to the town bull. Shall we

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: steal upon them, Ned, at supper?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: I am your shadow, my lord, I’ll follow you.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Sirrah, you boy, and Bardolph, no word to your master that I am yet

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: come to town. There’s for your silence.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: I have no tongue, sir.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: And for mine, sir, I will govern it.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Fare you well; go.
[_Exeunt Bardolph and Page._]

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: This Doll Tearsheet should be some road.

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: I warrant you, as common as the way between Saint Albans and London.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: How might we see Falstaff bestow himself tonight in his true colours,

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: and not ourselves be seen?

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: Put on two leathern jerkins and aprons, and wait upon him at his table

lines.speaker: POINS
lines.text: as drawers.

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: From a god to a bull? A heavy descension! It was Jove’s case. From a

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: prince to a ’prentice? A low transformation that shall be mine, for in

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: everything the purpose must weigh with the folly. Follow me, Ned.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Northumberland, Lady Northumberland and Lady Percy.

lines.text: I pray thee, loving wife, and gentle daughter,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Give even way unto my rough affairs;

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Put not you on the visage of the times

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And be like them to Percy troublesome.

lines.speaker: LADY NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: I have given over, I will speak no more.

lines.speaker: LADY NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Do what you will; your wisdom be your guide.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Alas, sweet wife, my honour is at pawn,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And, but my going, nothing can redeem it.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: O yet, for God’s sake, go not to these wars!

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: The time was, father, that you broke your word,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: When you were more endear’d to it than now;

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: When your own Percy, when my heart’s dear Harry,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Threw many a northward look to see his father

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Bring up his powers; but he did long in vain.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Who then persuaded you to stay at home?

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: There were two honours lost, yours and your son’s.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: For yours, the God of heaven brighten it!

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: For his, it stuck upon him as the sun

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: In the grey vault of heaven, and by his light

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Did all the chivalry of England move

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: To do brave acts. He was indeed the glass

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Wherein the noble youth did dress themselves.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: He had no legs that practis’d not his gait;

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: And speaking thick, which nature made his blemish,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Became the accents of the valiant;

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: For those who could speak low and tardily

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Would turn their own perfection to abuse,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: To seem like him. So that in speech, in gait,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: In diet, in affections of delight,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: In military rules, humours of blood,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: He was the mark and glass, copy and book,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: That fashion’d others. And him—O wondrous him!

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: O miracle of men!—him did you leave,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Second to none, unseconded by you,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: To look upon the hideous god of war

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: In disadvantage, to abide a field

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Where nothing but the sound of Hotspur’s name

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Did seem defensible: so you left him.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Never, O never, do his ghost the wrong

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: To hold your honour more precise and nice

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: With others than with him! Let them alone.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: The Marshal and the Archbishop are strong:

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Had my sweet Harry had but half their numbers,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Today might I, hanging on Hotspur’s neck,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Have talk’d of Monmouth’s grave.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Beshrew your heart,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Fair daughter, you do draw my spirits from me

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: With new lamenting ancient oversights.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: But I must go and meet with danger there,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Or it will seek me in another place,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And find me worse provided.

lines.speaker: LADY NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: O, fly to Scotland,

lines.speaker: LADY NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Till that the nobles and the armed commons

lines.speaker: LADY NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Have of their puissance made a little taste.

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: If they get ground and vantage of the King,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: Then join you with them like a rib of steel,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: To make strength stronger; but, for all our loves,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: First let them try themselves. So did your son;

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: He was so suffer’d. So came I a widow,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: And never shall have length of life enough

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: To rain upon remembrance with mine eyes,

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: That it may grow and sprout as high as heaven

lines.speaker: LADY PERCY
lines.text: For recordation to my noble husband.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Come, come, go in with me. ’Tis with my mind

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: As with the tide swell’d up unto his height,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: That makes a still-stand, running neither way.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Fain would I go to meet the Archbishop,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: But many thousand reasons hold me back.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: I will resolve for Scotland. There am I,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Till time and vantage crave my company.
[_Exeunt._]

lines.text: If he swagger, let him not come here. No, by my faith, I must live

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: with the very best. Shut the door, there comes no swaggerers here. I

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: have not lived all this while to have swaggering now. Shut the door, I

lines.speaker: HOSTESS
lines.text: pray you.

lines.text: Dost thou hear, hostess?

lines.text: Pray ye pacify yourself, Sir John. There comes no swaggerers here.

lines.text: Tilly-fally, Sir John, ne’er tell me. And our ancient swaggerer comes

lines.text: Therefore take heed what guests you receive. Receive,” says he, “no
