lines.speaker: SILENCE
lines.text: Your good worship is welcome.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Fie, this is hot weather, gentlemen. Have you provided me here half a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: dozen sufficient men?

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Marry, have we, sir. Will you sit?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Let me see them, I beseech you.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Where’s the roll? Where’s the roll? Where’s the roll? Let me see, let

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: me see, let me see. So, so, so, so, so, so, so. Yea, marry, sir: Ralph

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Mouldy! Let them appear as I call; let them do so, let them do so. Let

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: me see; where is Mouldy?

lines.speaker: MOULDY
lines.text: Here, an it please you.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: What think you, Sir John? A good-limbed fellow, young, strong, and of

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: good friends.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Is thy name Mouldy?

lines.speaker: MOULDY
lines.text: Yea, an’t please you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ’Tis the more time thou wert used.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Ha, ha, ha! most excellent, i’ faith! Things that are mouldy lack use.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Very singular good, in faith, well said, Sir John, very well said.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Prick him.

lines.speaker: MOULDY
lines.text: I was pricked well enough before, an you could have let me alone. My

lines.speaker: MOULDY
lines.text: old dame will be undone now for one to do her husbandry and her

lines.speaker: MOULDY
lines.text: drudgery. You need not to have pricked me, there are other men fitter

lines.speaker: MOULDY
lines.text: to go out than I.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Go to. Peace, Mouldy; you shall go. Mouldy, it is time you were spent.

lines.speaker: MOULDY
lines.text: Spent?

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Peace, fellow, peace. Stand aside. Know you where you are? For

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: th’other, Sir John. Let me see: Simon Shadow!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Yea, marry, let me have him to sit under. He’s like to be a cold

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: soldier.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Where’s Shadow?

lines.speaker: SHADOW
lines.text: Here, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Shadow, whose son art thou?

lines.speaker: SHADOW
lines.text: My mother’s son, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Thy mother’s son! Like enough, and thy father’s shadow. So the son of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the female is the shadow of the male. It is often so indeed, but much

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: of the father’s substance!

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Do you like him, Sir John?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Shadow will serve for summer. Prick him, for we have a number of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shadows to fill up the muster-book.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Thomas Wart!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Where’s he?

lines.speaker: WART
lines.text: Here, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Is thy name Wart?

lines.speaker: WART
lines.text: Yea, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Thou art a very ragged wart.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Shall I prick him, Sir John?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: It were superfluous, for his apparel is built upon his back, and the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: whole frame stands upon pins. Prick him no more.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Ha, ha, ha! You can do it, sir, you can do it. I commend you well.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Francis Feeble!

lines.speaker: FEEBLE
lines.text: Here, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What trade art thou, Feeble?

lines.speaker: FEEBLE
lines.text: A woman’s tailor, sir.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Shall I prick him, sir?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: You may; but if he had been a man’s tailor, he’d ha’ pricked you. Wilt

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: thou make as many holes in an enemy’s battle as thou hast done in a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: woman’s petticoat?

lines.speaker: FEEBLE
lines.text: I will do my good will, sir, you can have no more.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well said, good woman’s tailor! Well said, courageous Feeble! Thou wilt

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: be as valiant as the wrathful dove or most magnanimous mouse. Prick the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: woman’s tailor: well, Master Shallow, deep, Master Shallow.

lines.speaker: FEEBLE
lines.text: I would Wart might have gone, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I would thou wert a man’s tailor, that thou mightst mend him and make

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: him fit to go. I cannot put him to a private soldier that is the leader

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: of so many thousands. Let that suffice, most forcible Feeble.

lines.speaker: FEEBLE
lines.text: It shall suffice, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I am bound to thee, reverend Feeble. Who is next?

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Peter Bullcalf o’ th’ green!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Yea, marry, let’s see Bullcalf.

lines.speaker: BULLCALF
lines.text: Here, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Fore God, a likely fellow! Come, prick me Bullcalf till he roar again.

lines.speaker: BULLCALF
lines.text: O Lord! good my lord captain—

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What, dost thou roar before thou art pricked?

lines.speaker: BULLCALF
lines.text: O Lord, sir, I am a diseased man.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What disease hast thou?

lines.speaker: BULLCALF
lines.text: A whoreson cold, sir, a cough, sir, which I caught with ringing in the

lines.speaker: BULLCALF
lines.text: King’s affairs upon his coronation day, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Come, thou shalt go to the wars in a gown; we will have away thy cold,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and I will take such order that thy friends shall ring for thee. Is

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: here all?

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Here is two more called than your number; you must have but four here,

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: sir; and so, I pray you, go in with me to dinner.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Come, I will go drink with you, but I cannot tarry dinner. I am glad to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: see you, by my troth, Master Shallow.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: O, Sir John, do you remember since we lay all night in the windmill in

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Saint George’s Field?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: No more of that, good Master Shallow, no more of that.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Ha, ’twas a merry night. And is Jane Nightwork alive?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: She lives, Master Shallow.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: She never could away with me.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Never, never; she would always say she could not abide Master Shallow.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: By the mass, I could anger her to th’ heart. She was then a bona-roba.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Doth she hold her own well?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Old, old, Master Shallow.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Nay, she must be old, she cannot choose but be old, certain she’s old,

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: and had Robin Nightwork by old Nightwork before I came to Clement’s

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Inn.

lines.speaker: SILENCE
lines.text: That’s fifty-five year ago.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Ha, cousin Silence, that thou hadst seen that that this knight and I

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: have seen! Ha, Sir John, said I well?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: We have heard the chimes at midnight, Master Shallow.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: That we have, that we have, that we have; in faith, Sir John, we have.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Our watchword was “Hem boys!” Come, let’s to dinner; come, let’s to

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: dinner. Jesus, the days that we have seen! Come, come.
[_Exeunt Falstaff, Shallow and Silence._]

lines.speaker: BULLCALF
lines.text: Good Master Corporate Bardolph, stand my friend; and here’s four Harry

lines.speaker: BULLCALF
lines.text: ten shillings in French crowns for you. In very truth, sir, I had as

lines.speaker: BULLCALF
lines.text: lief be hanged, sir, as go. And yet, for mine own part, sir, I do not

lines.speaker: BULLCALF
lines.text: care; but rather because I am unwilling, and, for mine own part, have a

lines.speaker: BULLCALF
lines.text: desire to stay with my friends; else, sir, I did not care, for mine own

lines.speaker: BULLCALF
lines.text: part, so much.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Go to, stand aside.

lines.speaker: MOULDY
lines.text: And, good Master Corporal Captain, for my old dame’s sake, stand my

lines.speaker: MOULDY
lines.text: friend. She has nobody to do anything about her when I am gone, and she

lines.speaker: MOULDY
lines.text: is old, and cannot help herself. You shall have forty, sir.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Go to, stand aside.

lines.speaker: FEEBLE
lines.text: By my troth, I care not. A man can die but once. We owe God a death.

lines.speaker: FEEBLE
lines.text: I’ll ne’er bear a base mind. An ’t be my destiny, so; an ’t be not, so.

lines.speaker: FEEBLE
lines.text: No man’s too good to serve’s prince, and let it go which way it will,

lines.speaker: FEEBLE
lines.text: he that dies this year is quit for the next.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Well said, th’art a good fellow.

lines.speaker: FEEBLE
lines.text: Faith, I’ll bear no base mind.
Enter Falstaff and the Justices.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Come, sir, which men shall I have?

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Four of which you please.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Sir, a word with you. I have three pound to free Mouldy and Bullcalf.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Go to, well.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Come, Sir John, which four will you have?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Do you choose for me.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Marry, then, Mouldy, Bullcalf, Feeble, and Shadow.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Mouldy and Bullcalf: for you, Mouldy, stay at home till you are past

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: service; and for your part, Bullcalf, grow till you come unto it. I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: will none of you.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Sir John, Sir John, do not yourself wrong. They are your likeliest men,

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: and I would have you served with the best.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Will you tell me, Master Shallow, how to choose a man? Care I for the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: limb, the thews, the stature, bulk, and big assemblance of a man? Give

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: me the spirit, Master Shallow. Here’s Wart. You see what a ragged

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: appearance it is. He shall charge you and discharge you with the motion

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: of a pewterer’s hammer, come off and on swifter than he that gibbets on

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the brewer’s bucket. And this same half-faced fellow, Shadow; give me

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: this man. He presents no mark to the enemy. The foeman may with as

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: great aim level at the edge of a penknife. And for a retreat, how

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: swiftly will this Feeble, the woman’s tailor, run off! O, give me the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: spare men, and spare me the great ones. Put me a caliver into Wart’s

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hand, Bardolph.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Hold, Wart. Traverse. Thas, thas, thas.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Come, manage me your caliver. So, very well, go to, very good,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: exceeding good. O, give me always a little, lean, old, chopt, bald

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shot. Well said, i’ faith, Wart. Th’art a good scab. Hold, there’s a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: tester for thee.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: He is not his craft’s master, he doth not do it right. I remember at

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Mile-End Green, when I lay at Clement’s Inn—I was then Sir Dagonet in

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Arthur’s show—there was a little quiver fellow, and he would manage you

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: his piece thus. And he would about and about, and come you in and come

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: you in. “Rah, tah, tah,” would he say. “Bounce” would he say; and away

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: again would he go, and again would he come. I shall ne’er see such a

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: fellow.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: These fellows will do well. Master Shallow. God keep you, Master

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Silence: I will not use many words with you. Fare you well, gentlemen

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: both. I thank you. I must a dozen mile tonight. Bardolph, give the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: soldiers coats.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Sir John, the Lord bless you! God prosper your affairs! God send us

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: peace! At your return, visit our house, let our old acquaintance be

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: renewed. Peradventure I will with ye to the court.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Fore God, I would you would, Master Shallow.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Go to, I have spoke at a word. God keep you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Fare you well, gentle gentlemen. [_Exeunt Justices_.] On, Bardolph,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: lead the men away. [_Exeunt Bardolph, recruits, &c._] As I return, I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: will fetch off these justices. I do see the bottom of Justice Shallow.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Lord, Lord, how subject we old men are to this vice of lying! This same

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: starved justice hath done nothing but prate to me of the wildness of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: his youth, and the feats he hath done about Turnbull Street, and every

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: third word a lie, duer paid to the hearer than the Turk’s tribute. I do

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: remember him at Clement’s Inn, like a man made after supper of a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cheese-paring. When he was naked, he was, for all the world, like a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: forked radish, with a head fantastically carved upon it with a knife.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: He was so forlorn, that his dimensions to any thick sight were

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: invincible. He was the very genius of famine, yet lecherous as a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: monkey, and the whores called him mandrake. He came ever in the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: rearward of the fashion, and sung those tunes to the overscutched

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: huswives that he heard the carmen whistle, and sware they were his

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: fancies or his good-nights. And now is this Vice’s dagger become a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: squire, and talks as familiarly of John a Gaunt as if he had been sworn

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: brother to him, and I’ll be sworn he ne’er saw him but once in the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: tilt-yard, and then he burst his head for crowding among the marshal’s

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: men. I saw it and told John a Gaunt he beat his own name, for you might

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: have thrust him and all his apparel into an eel-skin; the case of a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: treble hautboy was a mansion for him, a court. And now has he land and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: beefs. Well, I’ll be acquainted with him if I return, and ’t shall go

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hard but I’ll make him a philosopher’s two stones to me. If the young

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: dace be a bait for the old pike, I see no reason in the law of nature

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: but I may snap at him. Let time shape, and there an end.
[_Exit._]
Enter the Archbishop of York, Mowbray, Hastings and others.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: What is this forest call’d?

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: ’Tis Gaultree Forest, an ’t shall please your Grace.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Here stand, my lords, and send discoverers forth

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: To know the numbers of our enemies.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: We have sent forth already.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: ’Tis well done.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: My friends and brethren in these great affairs,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: I must acquaint you that I have received

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: New-dated letters from Northumberland,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Their cold intent, tenor, and substance, thus:

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Here doth he wish his person, with such powers

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: As might hold sortance with his quality,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: The which he could not levy; whereupon

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: He is retired, to ripe his growing fortunes,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: To Scotland, and concludes in hearty prayers

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: That your attempts may overlive the hazard

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And fearful meeting of their opposite.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Thus do the hopes we have in him touch ground

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And dash themselves to pieces.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Now, what news?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: West of this forest, scarcely off a mile,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: In goodly form comes on the enemy,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And, by the ground they hide, I judge their number

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Upon or near the rate of thirty thousand.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: The just proportion that we gave them out.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Let us sway on and face them in the field.
Enter Westmoreland.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: What well-appointed leader fronts us here?

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: I think it is my Lord of Westmoreland.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Health and fair greeting from our general,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: The prince, Lord John and Duke of Lancaster.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Say on, my Lord of Westmoreland, in peace,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: What doth concern your coming.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Then, my lord,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Unto your Grace do I in chief address

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: The substance of my speech. If that rebellion

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Came like itself, in base and abject routs,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Led on by bloody youth, guarded with rags,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: And countenanced by boys and beggary;

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: I say, if damn’d commotion so appear’d

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: In his true, native, and most proper shape,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: You, reverend father, and these noble lords

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Had not been here to dress the ugly form

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Of base and bloody insurrection

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: With your fair honours. You, Lord Archbishop,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Whose see is by a civil peace maintain’d,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Whose beard the silver hand of peace hath touch’d,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Whose learning and good letters peace hath tutor’d,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Whose white investments figure innocence,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: The dove and very blessed spirit of peace,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Wherefore you do so ill translate yourself

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Out of the speech of peace that bears such grace,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Into the harsh and boisterous tongue of war;

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Turning your books to graves, your ink to blood,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Your pens to lances and your tongue divine

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: To a loud trumpet and a point of war?

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Wherefore do I this? So the question stands.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Briefly to this end: we are all diseased,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And with our surfeiting and wanton hours

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Have brought ourselves into a burning fever,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And we must bleed for it; of which disease

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Our late King Richard, being infected, died.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: But, my most noble Lord of Westmoreland,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: I take not on me here as a physician,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Nor do I as an enemy to peace

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Troop in the throngs of military men,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: But rather show awhile like fearful war

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: To diet rank minds sick of happiness,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And purge th’ obstructions which begin to stop

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Our very veins of life. Hear me more plainly.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: I have in equal balance justly weigh’d

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: What wrongs our arms may do, what wrongs we suffer,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And find our griefs heavier than our offences.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: We see which way the stream of time doth run,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And are enforced from our most quiet there

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: By the rough torrent of occasion,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And have the summary of all our griefs,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: When time shall serve, to show in articles;

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Which long ere this we offer’d to the King

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And might by no suit gain our audience.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: When we are wrong’d and would unfold our griefs,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: We are denied access unto his person

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Even by those men that most have done us wrong.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: The dangers of the days but newly gone,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Whose memory is written on the earth

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: With yet-appearing blood, and the examples

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Of every minute’s instance, present now,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Hath put us in these ill-beseeming arms,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Not to break peace or any branch of it,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: But to establish here a peace indeed,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Concurring both in name and quality.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Whenever yet was your appeal denied?

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Wherein have you been galled by the King?

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: What peer hath been suborn’d to grate on you,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: That you should seal this lawless bloody book

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Of forged rebellion with a seal divine

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: And consecrate commotion’s bitter edge?

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: My brother general, the commonwealth,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: To brother born an household cruelty,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: I make my quarrel in particular.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: There is no need of any such redress,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Or if there were, it not belongs to you.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Why not to him in part, and to us all

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: That feel the bruises of the days before,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And suffer the condition of these times

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: To lay a heavy and unequal hand

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Upon our honours?

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: O, my good Lord Mowbray,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Construe the times to their necessities,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: And you shall say indeed, it is the time,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: And not the King, that doth you injuries.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Yet for your part, it not appears to me

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Either from the King or in the present time

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: That you should have an inch of any ground

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: To build a grief on. Were you not restored

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: To all the Duke of Norfolk’s signories,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Your noble and right well rememb’red father’s?

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: What thing, in honour, had my father lost,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: That need to be revived and breathed in me?

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: The King that loved him, as the state stood then,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Was force perforce compell’d to banish him,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And then that Henry Bolingbroke and he,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Being mounted and both roused in their seats,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Their neighing coursers daring of the spur,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Their armed staves in charge, their beavers down,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Their eyes of fire sparkling through sights of steel,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And the loud trumpet blowing them together,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Then, then, when there was nothing could have stay’d

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: My father from the breast of Bolingbroke,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: O, when the King did throw his warder down,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: His own life hung upon the staff he threw;

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Then threw he down himself and all their lives

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: That by indictment and by dint of sword

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Have since miscarried under Bolingbroke.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: You speak, Lord Mowbray, now you know not what.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: The Earl of Hereford was reputed then

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: In England the most valiant gentleman.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Who knows on whom fortune would then have smiled?

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: But if your father had been victor there,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: He ne’er had borne it out of Coventry;

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: For all the country in a general voice

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Cried hate upon him; and all their prayers and love

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Were set on Hereford, whom they doted on

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: And bless’d and graced, indeed more than the King.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: But this is mere digression from my purpose.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Here come I from our princely general

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: To know your griefs, to tell you from his Grace

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: That he will give you audience; and wherein

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: It shall appear that your demands are just,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: You shall enjoy them, everything set off

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: That might so much as think you enemies.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: But he hath forc’d us to compel this offer,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And it proceeds from policy, not love.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Mowbray, you overween to take it so;

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: This offer comes from mercy, not from fear.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: For, lo, within a ken our army lies,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Upon mine honour, all too confident

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: To give admittance to a thought of fear.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Our battle is more full of names than yours,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Our men more perfect in the use of arms,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Our armour all as strong, our cause the best;

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Then reason will our hearts should be as good.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Say you not then our offer is compell’d.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Well, by my will we shall admit no parley.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: That argues but the shame of your offence:

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: A rotten case abides no handling.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Hath the Prince John a full commission,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: In very ample virtue of his father,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: To hear and absolutely to determine

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Of what conditions we shall stand upon?

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: That is intended in the general’s name:

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: I muse you make so slight a question.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Then take, my Lord of Westmoreland, this schedule,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: For this contains our general grievances.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Each several article herein redress’d,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: All members of our cause, both here and hence,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: That are insinew’d to this action,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Acquitted by a true substantial form

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And present execution of our wills

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: To us and to our purposes confined,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: We come within our awful banks again

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And knit our powers to the arm of peace.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: This will I show the general. Please you, lords,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: In sight of both our battles we may meet,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: And either end in peace, which God so frame!

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Or to the place of difference call the swords

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Which must decide it.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: My lord, we will do so.
[_Exit Westmoreland._]

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: There is a thing within my bosom tells me

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: That no conditions of our peace can stand.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Fear you not that: if we can make our peace

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Upon such large terms and so absolute

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: As our conditions shall consist upon,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Our peace shall stand as firm as rocky mountains.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Yea, but our valuation shall be such

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: That every slight and false-derived cause,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Yea, every idle, nice, and wanton reason,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Shall to the King taste of this action;

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: That, were our royal faiths martyrs in love,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: We shall be winnow’d with so rough a wind

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: That even our corn shall seem as light as chaff

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And good from bad find no partition.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: No, no, my lord. Note this; the King is weary

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Of dainty and such picking grievances;

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: For he hath found to end one doubt by death

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Revives two greater in the heirs of life;

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And therefore will he wipe his tables clean

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And keep no tell-tale to his memory

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: That may repeat and history his loss

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: To new remembrance. For full well he knows

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: He cannot so precisely weed this land

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: As his misdoubts present occasion.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: His foes are so enrooted with his friends

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: That, plucking to unfix an enemy,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: He doth unfasten so and shake a friend.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: So that this land, like an offensive wife

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: That hath enraged him on to offer strokes,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: As he is striking, holds his infant up

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And hangs resolved correction in the arm

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: That was uprear’d to execution.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Besides, the King hath wasted all his rods

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: On late offenders, that he now doth lack

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: The very instruments of chastisement;

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: So that his power, like to a fangless lion,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: May offer, but not hold.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: ’Tis very true,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And therefore be assured, my good Lord Marshal,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: If we do now make our atonement well,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Our peace will, like a broken limb united,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Grow stronger for the breaking.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Be it so.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Here is return’d my Lord of Westmoreland.
Enter Westmoreland.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: The prince is here at hand. Pleaseth your lordship

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: To meet his Grace just distance ’tween our armies.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Your Grace of York, in God’s name then set forward.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Before, and greet his Grace. My lord, we come.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter, from one side, Mowbray, attended; afterwards, the Archbishop, Hastings, and others; from the other side, Prince John of Lancaster, and Westmoreland; Officers, and others with them.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: You are well encounter’d here, my cousin Mowbray.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Good day to you, gentle Lord Archbishop;

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: And so to you, Lord Hastings, and to all.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: My Lord of York, it better show’d with you

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: When that your flock, assembled by the bell,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Encircled you to hear with reverence

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Your exposition on the holy text

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Than now to see you here an iron man,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Cheering a rout of rebels with your drum,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Turning the word to sword, and life to death.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: That man that sits within a monarch’s heart,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: And ripens in the sunshine of his favour,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Would he abuse the countenance of the king,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Alack, what mischiefs might he set abroach

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: In shadow of such greatness! With you, Lord Bishop,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: It is even so. Who hath not heard it spoken

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: How deep you were within the books of God,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: To us the speaker in his parliament,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: To us th’ imagined voice of God himself,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: The very opener and intelligencer

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Between the grace, the sanctities of heaven,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: And our dull workings? O, who shall believe

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: But you misuse the reverence of your place,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Employ the countenance and grace of heaven

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: As a false favourite doth his prince’s name,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: In deeds dishonourable? You have ta’en up,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Under the counterfeited zeal of God,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: The subjects of his substitute, my father,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: And both against the peace of heaven and him

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Have here up-swarm’d them.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Good my Lord of Lancaster,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: I am not here against your father’s peace;

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: But, as I told my Lord of Westmoreland,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: The time misorder’d doth, in common sense,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Crowd us and crush us to this monstrous form

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: To hold our safety up. I sent your Grace

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: The parcels and particulars of our grief,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: The which hath been with scorn shoved from the court,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Whereon this Hydra son of war is born,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Whose dangerous eyes may well be charm’d asleep

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: With grant of our most just and right desires,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And true obedience, of this madness cured,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Stoop tamely to the foot of majesty.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: If not, we ready are to try our fortunes

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: To the last man.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And though we here fall down,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: We have supplies to second our attempt:

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: If they miscarry, theirs shall second them;

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And so success of mischief shall be born,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: And heir from heir shall hold this quarrel up

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Whiles England shall have generation.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: You are too shallow, Hastings, much too shallow,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: To sound the bottom of the after-times.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Pleaseth your Grace to answer them directly

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: How far forth you do like their articles.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: I like them all, and do allow them well,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: And swear here, by the honour of my blood,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: My father’s purposes have been mistook,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: And some about him have too lavishly

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Wrested his meaning and authority.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: My lord, these griefs shall be with speed redress’d;

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Upon my soul, they shall. If this may please you,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Discharge your powers unto their several counties,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: As we will ours; and here between the armies

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Let’s drink together friendly and embrace,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: That all their eyes may bear those tokens home

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Of our restored love and amity.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: I take your princely word for these redresses.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: I give it you, and will maintain my word;

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: And thereupon I drink unto your Grace.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Go, captain, and deliver to the army

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: This news of peace. Let them have pay, and part.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: I know it will please them. Hie thee, captain.
[_Exit Officer._]

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: To you, my noble Lord of Westmoreland.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: I pledge your Grace; and if you knew what pains

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: I have bestow’d to breed this present peace,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: You would drink freely; but my love to ye

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Shall show itself more openly hereafter.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: I do not doubt you.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: I am glad of it.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Health to my lord and gentle cousin, Mowbray.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: You wish me health in very happy season,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: For I am on the sudden something ill.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Against ill chances men are ever merry,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: But heaviness foreruns the good event.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Therefore be merry, coz, since sudden sorrow

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Serves to say thus, “Some good thing comes tomorrow.”

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Believe me, I am passing light in spirit.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: So much the worse, if your own rule be true.
[_Shouts within._]

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: The word of peace is render’d. Hark how they shout!

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: This had been cheerful after victory.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: A peace is of the nature of a conquest;

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: For then both parties nobly are subdued,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And neither party loser.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Go, my lord.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: And let our army be discharged too.
[_Exit Westmoreland._]

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: And, good my lord, so please you, let our trains

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: March by us, that we may peruse the men

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: We should have coped withal.

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Go, good Lord Hastings,

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: And, ere they be dismiss’d, let them march by.
[_Exit Hastings._]

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: I trust, lords, we shall lie tonight together.
Enter Westmoreland.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Now, cousin, wherefore stands our army still?

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: The leaders, having charge from you to stand,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Will not go off until they hear you speak.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: They know their duties.
Enter Hastings.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: My lord, our army is dispersed already.

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Like youthful steers unyoked, they take their courses

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: East, west, north, south; or, like a school broke up,

lines.speaker: HASTINGS
lines.text: Each hurries toward his home and sporting-place.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Good tidings, my Lord Hastings; for the which

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: I do arrest thee, traitor, of high treason;

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: And you, Lord Archbishop, and you, Lord Mowbray,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Of capital treason I attach you both.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Is this proceeding just and honourable?

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Is your assembly so?

lines.speaker: ARCHBISHOP
lines.text: Will you thus break your faith?

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: I pawn’d thee none.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: I promised you redress of these same grievances

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Whereof you did complain; which, by mine honour,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: I will perform with a most Christian care.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: But for you, rebels, look to taste the due

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Meet for rebellion and such acts as yours.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Most shallowly did you these arms commence,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Fondly brought here and foolishly sent hence.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Strike up our drums, pursue the scattr’d stray:

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: God, and not we, hath safely fought today.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Some guard these traitors to the block of death,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Treason’s true bed and yielder-up of breath.
[_Exeunt._]
Alarum. Excursions. Enter Falstaff and Colevile, meeting.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What’s your name, sir? Of what condition are you, and of what place, I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: pray?

lines.speaker: COLEVILE
lines.text: I am a knight, sir, and my name is Colevile of the Dale.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, then, Colevile is your name, a knight is your degree, and your

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: place the Dale. Colevile shall be still your name, a traitor your

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: degree, and the dungeon your place, a place deep enough; so shall you

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: be still Colevile of the Dale.

lines.speaker: COLEVILE
lines.text: Are not you Sir John Falstaff?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: As good a man as he, sir, whoe’er I am. Do ye yield, sir, or shall I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: sweat for you? If I do sweat, they are the drops of thy lovers, and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: they weep for thy death. Therefore rouse up fear and trembling, and do

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: observance to my mercy.

lines.speaker: COLEVILE
lines.text: I think you are Sir John Falstaff, and in that thought yield me.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I have a whole school of tongues in this belly of mine, and not a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: tongue of them all speaks any other word but my name. An I had but a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: belly of any indifferency, I were simply the most active fellow in

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Europe. My womb, my womb, my womb undoes me. Here comes our general.
Enter Prince John of Lancaster, Westmoreland, Blunt, and others.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: The heat is past; follow no further now.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Call in the powers, good cousin Westmoreland.
[_Exit Westmoreland._]

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Now, Falstaff, where have you been all this while?

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: When everything is ended, then you come.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: These tardy tricks of yours will, on my life,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: One time or other break some gallows’ back.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I would be sorry, my lord, but it should be thus. I never knew yet but

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: rebuke and check was the reward of valour. Do you think me a swallow,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: an arrow, or a bullet? Have I, in my poor and old motion, the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: expedition of thought? I have speeded hither with the very extremest

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: inch of possibility; I have foundered nine score and odd posts; and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: here, travel-tainted as I am, have in my pure and immaculate valour,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: taken Sir John Colevile of the Dale, a most furious knight and valorous

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: enemy. But what of that? He saw me, and yielded; that I may justly say,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: with the hook-nosed fellow of Rome, “I came, saw, and overcame.”

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: It was more of his courtesy than your deserving.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I know not. Here he is, and here I yield him. And I beseech your Grace,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: let it be booked with the rest of this day’s deeds, or, by the Lord, I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: will have it in a particular ballad else, with mine own picture on the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: top on’t, Colevile kissing my foot: to the which course if I be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: enforced, if you do not all show like gilt twopences to me, and I in

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the clear sky of fame o’ershine you as much as the full moon doth the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cinders of the element, which show like pins’ heads to her, believe not

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the word of the noble. Therefore let me have right, and let desert

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: mount.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Thine’s too heavy to mount.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Let it shine, then.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Thine’s too thick to shine.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Let it do something, my good lord, that may do me good, and call it

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: what you will.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Is thy name Colevile?

lines.speaker: COLEVILE
lines.text: It is, my lord.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: A famous rebel art thou, Colevile.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: And a famous true subject took him.

lines.speaker: COLEVILE
lines.text: I am, my lord, but as my betters are

lines.speaker: COLEVILE
lines.text: That led me hither. Had they been ruled by me,

lines.speaker: COLEVILE
lines.text: You should have won them dearer than you have.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I know not how they sold themselves, but thou, like a kind fellow,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: gavest thyself away gratis, and I thank thee for thee.
Enter Westmoreland.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Now, have you left pursuit?

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Retreat is made and execution stay’d.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Send Colevile with his confederates

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: To York, to present execution.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Blunt, lead him hence, and see you guard him sure.
[_Exeunt Blunt and others with Colevile._]

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: And now dispatch we toward the court, my lords.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: I hear the King my father is sore sick.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Our news shall go before us to his Majesty,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Which, cousin, you shall bear to comfort him,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: And we with sober speed will follow you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My lord, I beseech you give me leave to go through Gloucestershire,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and, when you come to court, stand my good lord, pray, in your good

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: report.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Fare you well, Falstaff. I, in my condition,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Shall better speak of you than you deserve.
[_Exeunt all but Falstaff._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I would you had but the wit, ’twere better than your dukedom. Good

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: faith, this same young sober-blooded boy doth not love me, nor a man

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cannot make him laugh; but that’s no marvel, he drinks no wine. There’s

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: never none of these demure boys come to any proof; for thin drink doth

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: so over-cool their blood, and making many fish meals, that they fall

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: into a kind of male green-sickness; and then, when they marry, they get

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: wenches. They are generally fools and cowards, which some of us should

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: be too, but for inflammation. A good sherris-sack hath a two-fold

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: operation in it. It ascends me into the brain, dries me there all the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: foolish and dull and crudy vapours which environ it, makes it

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: apprehensive, quick, forgetive, full of nimble, fiery, and delectable

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shapes, which, delivered o’er to the voice, the tongue, which is the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: birth, becomes excellent wit. The second property of your excellent

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: sherris is the warming of the blood, which, before cold and settled,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: left the liver white and pale, which is the badge of pusillanimity and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cowardice. But the sherris warms it and makes it course from the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: inwards to the parts’ extremes. It illumineth the face, which as a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: beacon gives warning to all the rest of this little kingdom, man, to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: arm; and then the vital commoners and inland petty spirits muster me

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: all to their captain, the heart, who, great and puffed up with this

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: retinue, doth any deed of courage; and this valour comes of sherris. So

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: that skill in the weapon is nothing without sack, for that sets it

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: a-work; and learning a mere hoard of gold kept by a devil, till sack

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: commences it and sets it in act and use. Hereof comes it that Prince

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Harry is valiant; for the cold blood he did naturally inherit of his

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: father he hath, like lean, sterile and bare land, manured, husbanded

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and tilled with excellent endeavour of drinking good and good store of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: fertile sherris, that he is become very hot and valiant. If I had a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: thousand sons, the first humane principle I would teach them should be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: to forswear thin potations and to addict themselves to sack.
Enter Bardolph.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: How now, Bardolph?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: The army is discharged all and gone.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Let them go. I’ll through Gloucestershire, and there will I visit

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Master Robert Shallow, Esquire. I have him already tempering between my

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: finger and my thumb, and shortly will I seal with him. Come away.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the King, Warwick, Thomas Duke of Clarence and Humphrey Duke of Gloucester and others.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Now, lords, if God doth give successful end

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To this debate that bleedeth at our doors,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We will our youth lead on to higher fields

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And draw no swords but what are sanctified.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our navy is address’d, our power collected,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our substitutes in absence well invested,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And everything lies level to our wish.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Only we want a little personal strength;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And pause us till these rebels now afoot

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Come underneath the yoke of government.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Both which we doubt not but your Majesty

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Shall soon enjoy.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Humphrey, my son of Gloucester,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Where is the Prince your brother?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I think he’s gone to hunt, my lord, at Windsor.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And how accompanied?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I do not know, my lord.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Is not his brother Thomas of Clarence with him?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: No, my good lord, he is in presence here.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: What would my lord and father?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Nothing but well to thee, Thomas of Clarence.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: How chance thou art not with the Prince thy brother?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He loves thee, and thou dost neglect him, Thomas.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou hast a better place in his affection

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Than all thy brothers. Cherish it, my boy,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And noble offices thou mayst effect

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of mediation, after I am dead,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Between his greatness and thy other brethren.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Therefore omit him not, blunt not his love,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Nor lose the good advantage of his grace

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: By seeming cold or careless of his will;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For he is gracious, if he be observed,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He hath a tear for pity, and a hand

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Open as day for melting charity:

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Yet notwithstanding, being incensed, he’s flint,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As humorous as winter, and as sudden

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As flaws congealed in the spring of day.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: His temper therefore must be well observed.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Chide him for faults, and do it reverently,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: When you perceive his blood inclined to mirth;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But, being moody, give him time and scope,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Till that his passions, like a whale on ground,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Confound themselves with working. Learn this, Thomas,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And thou shalt prove a shelter to thy friends,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A hoop of gold to bind thy brothers in,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That the united vessel of their blood,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Mingled with venom of suggestion—

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As, force perforce, the age will pour it in—

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Shall never leak, though it do work as strong

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As aconitum or rash gunpowder.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: I shall observe him with all care and love.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Why art thou not at Windsor with him, Thomas?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: He is not there today; he dines in London.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And how accompanied? Canst thou tell that?

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: With Poins, and other his continual followers.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Most subject is the fattest soil to weeds,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And he, the noble image of my youth,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Is overspread with them; therefore my grief

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Stretches itself beyond the hour of death.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The blood weeps from my heart when I do shape

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In forms imaginary th’ unguided days

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And rotten times that you shall look upon

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: When I am sleeping with my ancestors.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For when his headstrong riot hath no curb,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: When rage and hot blood are his counsellors,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: When means and lavish manners meet together,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: O, with what wings shall his affections fly

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Towards fronting peril and opposed decay!

lines.text: My gracious lord, you look beyond him quite.

lines.text: The prince but studies his companions

lines.text: Like a strange tongue, wherein, to gain the language,

lines.text: ’Tis needful that the most immodest word

lines.text: Be looked upon and learned; which once attained,

lines.text: Your Highness knows, comes to no further use

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But to be known and hated. So, like gross terms,

lines.text: The Prince will, in the perfectness of time,

lines.text: Cast off his followers, and their memory

lines.text: Shall as a pattern or a measure live,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: By which his Grace must mete the lives of other,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Turning past evils to advantages.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: ’Tis seldom when the bee doth leave her comb

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In the dead carrion.
Enter Westmoreland.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Who’s here? Westmoreland?

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Health to my sovereign, and new happiness

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Added to that that I am to deliver!

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Prince John your son doth kiss your Grace’s hand.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Mowbray, the Bishop Scroop, Hastings and all

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Are brought to the correction of your law.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: There is not now a rebel’s sword unsheathed,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: But Peace puts forth her olive everywhere.

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: The manner how this action hath been borne

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: Here at more leisure may your Highness read,

lines.speaker: WESTMORELAND
lines.text: With every course in his particular.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: O Westmoreland, thou art a summer bird,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which ever in the haunch of winter sings

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The lifting up of day.
Enter Harcourt.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Look, here’s more news.

lines.text: From enemies heaven keep your Majesty;

lines.speaker: HARCOURT
lines.text: And when they stand against you, may they fall

lines.speaker: HARCOURT
lines.text: As those that I am come to tell you of!

lines.speaker: HARCOURT
lines.text: The Earl Northumberland and the Lord Bardolph,

lines.speaker: HARCOURT
lines.text: With a great power of English and of Scots,

lines.text: The manner and true order of the fight

lines.text: This packet, please it you, contains at large.

lines.text: And wherefore should these good news make me sick?

lines.text: Will Fortune never come with both hands full,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But write her fair words still in foulest letters?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: She either gives a stomach and no food—

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Such are the poor, in health; or else a feast

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And takes away the stomach—such are the rich,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That have abundance and enjoy it not.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I should rejoice now at this happy news,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And now my sight fails, and my brain is giddy.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: O me! Come near me, now I am much ill.

lines.text: Comfort, your Majesty!

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: O my royal father!

lines.text: My sovereign lord, cheer up yourself, look up.

lines.text: Be patient, princes; you do know these fits

lines.text: Stand from him, give him air; he’ll straight be well.

lines.text: No, no, he cannot long hold out these pangs.

lines.text: Hath wrought the mure that should confine it in

lines.text: So thin that life looks through and will break out.

lines.text: The people fear me, for they do observe

lines.text: Unfather’d heirs and loathly births of nature.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: The seasons change their manners, as the year

lines.text: Had found some months asleep and leap’d them over.

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: The river hath thrice flow’d, no ebb between,

lines.speaker: CLARENCE
lines.text: And the old folk, time’s doting chronicles,

lines.text: Say it did so a little time before

lines.text: That our great-grandsire, Edward, sick’d and died.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Speak lower, princes, for the King recovers.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: This apoplexy will certain be his end.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I pray you take me up, and bear me hence

lines.speaker: KING

lines.text: Let there be no noise made, my gentle friends,

lines.text: Unless some dull and favourable hand

lines.text: Who saw the Duke of Clarence?

lines.text: I am here, brother, full of heaviness.

lines.text: How now, rain within doors, and none abroad?

lines.text: How doth the King?

lines.text: Exceeding ill.

lines.text: Heard he the good news yet? Tell it him.

lines.text: He alt’red much upon the hearing it.

lines.text: Not so much noise, my lords. Sweet prince, speak low;

[_Exeunt all but the Prince._]

lines.text: Why doth the crown lie there upon his pillow,

lines.text: Being so troublesome a bedfellow?

lines.text: O polish’d perturbation! golden care!

lines.text: That keep’st the ports of slumber open wide

lines.text: To many a watchful night! Sleep with it now;

lines.text: When thou dost pinch thy bearer, thou dost sit

lines.speaker: PRINCE
lines.text: Like a rich armour worn in heat of day,

lines.text: That scald’st with safety. By his gates of breath

lines.text: Did he suspire, that light and weightless down

lines.text: Why did you leave me here alone, my lords?

lines.text: We left the Prince my brother here, my liege,

lines.text: To be again displaced; which to avoid,

lines.text: To lead out many to the Holy Land,

lines.text: Lest rest and lying still might make them look

lines.text: How I came by the crown, O God, forgive,

lines.text: My Lord Chief Justice, speak to that vain man.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Have you your wits? Know you what ’tis you speak?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My King! My Jove! I speak to thee, my heart!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I know thee not, old man. Fall to thy prayers.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: How ill white hairs becomes a fool and jester!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I have long dreamt of such a kind of man,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: So surfeit-swell’d, so old, and so profane;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But, being awaked, I do despise my dream.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Make less thy body hence, and more thy grace;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Leave gormandizing; know the grave doth gape

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For thee thrice wider than for other men.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Reply not to me with a fool-born jest.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Presume not that I am the thing I was;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For God doth know, so shall the world perceive,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That I have turn’d away my former self;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: So will I those that kept me company.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: When thou dost hear I am as I have been,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Approach me, and thou shalt be as thou wast,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The tutor and the feeder of my riots.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Till then I banish thee, on pain of death,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As I have done the rest of my misleaders,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Not to come near our person by ten mile.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For competence of life I will allow you,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That lack of means enforce you not to evils.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And, as we hear you do reform yourselves,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We will, according to your strengths and qualities,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Give you advancement. Be it your charge, my lord,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To see perform’d the tenor of our word.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Set on.
[_Exeunt King with his train._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Master Shallow, I owe you a thousand pounds.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Yea, marry, Sir John, which I beseech you to let me have home with me.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: That can hardly be, Master Shallow. Do not you grieve at this; I shall

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: be sent for in private to him. Look you, he must seem thus to the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: world. Fear not your advancements; I will be the man yet that shall

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: make you great.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: I cannot perceive how, unless you give me your doublet and stuff me out

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: with straw. I beseech you, good Sir John, let me have five hundred of

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: my thousand.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Sir, I will be as good as my word. This that you heard was but a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: colour.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: A colour that I fear you will die in, Sir John.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Fear no colours. Go with me to dinner. Come, Lieutenant Pistol; come,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Bardolph. I shall be sent for soon at night.
Enter the Lord Chief Justice and Prince John, Officers with them.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Go, carry Sir John Falstaff to the Fleet.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Take all his company along with him.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My lord, my lord,—

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: I cannot now speak. I will hear you soon.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: Take them away.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: _Si fortuna me tormenta, spero me contenta._
[_Exeunt all but Prince John and the Lord Chief Justice._]

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: I like this fair proceeding of the King’s.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: He hath intent his wonted followers

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Shall all be very well provided for,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: But all are banish’d till their conversations

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Appear more wise and modest to the world.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: And so they are.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: The King hath call’d his parliament, my lord.

lines.speaker: CHIEF JUSTICE
lines.text: He hath.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: I will lay odds that, ere this year expire,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: We bear our civil swords and native fire

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: As far as France. I heard a bird so sing,

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Whose music, to my thinking, pleased the King.

lines.speaker: LANCASTER
lines.text: Come, will you hence?
[_Exeunt._]

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: First my fear; then my curtsy; last my speech. My fear is your

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: displeasure; my curtsy, my duty; and my speech, to beg your pardons. If

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: you look for a good speech now, you undo me, for what I have to say is

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: of mine own making; and what indeed I should say will, I doubt, prove

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: mine own marring. But to the purpose, and so to the venture. Be it

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: known to you, as it is very well, I was lately here in the end of a

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: displeasing play, to pray your patience for it and to promise you a

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: better. I meant indeed to pay you with this; which, if like an ill

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: venture it come unluckily home, I break, and you, my gentle creditors,

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: lose. Here I promised you I would be, and here I commit my body to your

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: mercies. Bate me some, and I will pay you some, and, as most debtors

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: do, promise you infinitely.

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: If my tongue cannot entreat you to acquit me, will you command me to

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: use my legs? And yet that were but light payment, to dance out of your

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: debt. But a good conscience will make any possible satisfaction, and so

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: would I. All the gentlewomen here have forgiven me; if the gentlemen

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: will not, then the gentlemen do not agree with the gentlewomen, which

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: was never seen before in such an assembly.

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: One word more, I beseech you. If you be not too much cloyed with fat

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: meat, our humble author will continue the story, with Sir John in it,

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: and make you merry with fair Katharine of France; where, for anything I

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: know, Falstaff shall die of a sweat, unless already he be killed with

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: your hard opinions; for Oldcastle died a martyr, and this is not the

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: man. My tongue is weary; when my legs are too, I will bid you good

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: night.
